features.name: Gulf of Guinea
features.detail: Selected adjacent countries are listed; this is not a maritime-boundary claim.

features.name: Hudson Bay
features.detail: Selected adjacent countries are listed; this is not a maritime-boundary claim.

features.name: Caspian Sea
features.detail: An inland, enclosed body of water; commonly classed as the largest lake. It is not part of the world ocean.

features.name: Dead Sea
features.detail: A hypersaline inland lake. Its shores are a low-elevation geography landmark; it is not an ocean-connected sea.

features.name: Strait of Gibraltar
features.detail: Atlantic Ocean ↔ Mediterranean Sea; separates Europe and Africa.

features.name: Strait of Hormuz
features.detail: Persian Gulf ↔ Gulf of Oman; major energy-shipping chokepoint.

features.name: Bab el-Mandeb
features.detail: Red Sea ↔ Gulf of Aden; part of the route to the Suez Canal.

features.name: Strait of Malacca
features.detail: Andaman Sea ↔ Singapore Strait / South China Sea route; between the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra.

features.name: Singapore Strait
features.detail: Connects the Malacca route with the South China Sea; Singapore lies immediately north.

features.name: Bosphorus
features.detail: Black Sea ↔ Sea of Marmara; passes through Istanbul.

features.name: Dardanelles
features.detail: Sea of Marmara ↔ Aegean Sea; together with the Bosphorus forms the Turkish Straits route.

features.name: Bering Strait
features.detail: Bering Sea ↔ Chukchi Sea; separates Asia and North America.

features.name: Palk Strait
features.detail: Between southeastern India and northern Sri Lanka; connects the Bay of Bengal with Palk Bay.

features.name: Strait of Dover
features.detail: English Channel ↔ North Sea; between England and France.

features.name: Strait of Magellan
features.detail: Atlantic ↔ Pacific route through southern Chile, north of Tierra del Fuego.

features.name: Drake Passage
features.detail: Between Cape Horn and the Antarctic Peninsula; connects the Atlantic and Pacific sectors of the Southern Ocean.

features.name: Sunda Strait
features.detail: Java Sea ↔ Indian Ocean; between Java and Sumatra.

features.name: Lombok Strait
features.detail: Between Bali and Lombok; a deep-water Indonesian passage.

features.name: Taiwan Strait
features.detail: Between mainland China and Taiwan; links the East and South China Sea regions.

features.name: Korea Strait
features.detail: Between southern Korea and Japan; leads to the Sea of Japan / East Sea.

features.name: Strait of Otranto
features.detail: Adriatic Sea ↔ Ionian Sea; between Italy and Albania.

features.name: Strait of Messina
features.detail: Between Sicily and mainland Italy.

features.name: Bass Strait
features.detail: Between Tasmania and mainland Australia.

features.name: Torres Strait
features.detail: Between Cape York Peninsula and New Guinea.

features.name: Cook Strait
features.detail: Between New Zealand's North and South Islands.

features.name: Strait of Tiran
features.detail: Entrance to the Gulf of Aqaba from the Red Sea.

features.name: Strait of Kerch
features.detail: Black Sea ↔ Sea of Azov; near Crimea, whose sovereignty and control are disputed.

features.name: Strait of Bonifacio
features.detail: Between Corsica and Sardinia.

features.name: Strait of Juan de Fuca
features.detail: Pacific entrance to the Salish Sea; between Vancouver Island and Washington.

features.name: Suez Canal
features.detail: Mediterranean Sea ↔ Red Sea; Egypt; opened in 1869.

features.name: Panama Canal
features.detail: Atlantic / Caribbean side ↔ Pacific Ocean; Panama; opened in 1914.

features.name: Kiel Canal
features.detail: North Sea ↔ Baltic Sea; Germany; opened in 1895.

features.name: Corinth Canal
features.detail: Gulf of Corinth ↔ Saronic Gulf; Greece; opened in 1893.

features.name: Suez / Panama comparison
features.detail: BCS cue: Suez joins the Mediterranean and Red seas; Panama connects Atlantic and Pacific routes. Neither is a natural strait.

features.name: Line of Control
features.detail: Military control line in Jammu and Kashmir; not a final international border. Marker is approximate; consult the UN map for the route.

features.name: Line of Actual Control
features.detail: India–China control-line concept; alignment is disputed and not mutually agreed in all sectors. Marker gives regional location only.

features.name: McMahon Line
features.detail: Boundary proposed in 1914 in the eastern Himalayas; disputed between India and China. Location marker only.

features.name: Radcliffe Line — west
features.detail: 1947 partition boundary in Punjab; distinguish it from the Line of Control in Kashmir.

features.name: Radcliffe Line — east
features.detail: 1947 partition boundary in Bengal; later agreements adjusted parts of the India–Bangladesh boundary.

features.name: Durand Line
features.detail: 1893 Afghanistan–British India boundary agreement; associated with the Afghanistan–Pakistan border and contested historically.

features.name: Korean Demilitarized Zone
features.detail: 1953 armistice zone around the Military Demarcation Line. It does not simply follow the 38th parallel.

features.name: 38th parallel north
features.detail: Historical 1945 division reference for Korea. The present demarcation line differs from this latitude.

features.name: 49th parallel north
features.detail: Forms much of the western Canada–US boundary, not the entire border.

features.name: 17th parallel north
features.detail: Historical reference for the provisional Vietnam division under the 1954 Geneva arrangements; not a current national boundary.

features.name: 22nd parallel north
features.detail: Associated with the 1899 Egypt–Sudan boundary; the Hala'ib and Bir Tawil areas require the separate 1902 administrative-line context.

features.name: 31st parallel north
features.detail: Latitude reference requested for study. It is not a universal named border; consult the applicable treaty for any border segment.

features.name: Green Line — Cyprus
features.detail: UN buffer-zone context between the island's communities; not a recognised international border.

features.name: Green Line — 1949 armistice
features.detail: 1949 armistice demarcation reference; distinguish it from final-status international boundaries.

features.name: Blue Line
features.detail: UN withdrawal-verification line established in 2000; not an agreed international border.

features.name: Oder–Neisse line
features.detail: Name associated with the Germany–Poland boundary along the Oder and Lusatian Neisse rivers.

features.name: Maginot Line
features.detail: Historical French defensive fortifications; not a political boundary.

features.name: Mason–Dixon line
features.detail: Historical surveyed boundary associated chiefly with Pennsylvania and Maryland; not an international border.

features.name: India–Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement
features.detail: 1974 agreement and 2011 protocol implemented in 2015; exchange involved 111 Indian and 51 Bangladeshi enclaves.

features.name: Ganges / Padma
features.detail: Ganges enters Bangladesh, where its main channel is called Padma; major component of the Bengal delta.

features.name: Brahmaputra / Jamuna
features.detail: Originates on the Tibetan Plateau; known as Yarlung Tsangpo upstream and Jamuna for the main Bangladesh channel.

features.name: Meghna
features.detail: Major Bangladesh river system draining to the Bay of Bengal; the Barak system is an important upstream component.

features.name: Teesta River
features.detail: Himalayan transboundary river; an important Bangladesh–India water-sharing topic.

features.name: Naf River
features.detail: Part of the Bangladesh–Myanmar boundary near the Bay of Bengal.

features.name: Halda River
features.detail: Originates within Bangladesh; an important natural carp-spawning river.

features.name: Sundarbans
features.detail: Mangrove forest across Bangladesh and India. The Bangladesh World Heritage property was inscribed in 1997.

features.name: Chattogram
features.detail: Major Bangladesh seaport; Chittagong is the older English spelling.

features.name: Mongla
features.detail: Bangladesh seaport near the Sundarbans.

features.name: Payra Port
features.detail: Bangladesh seaport in Patuakhali district.

features.name: Saint Martin's Island
features.detail: Island in the northeastern Bay of Bengal near the Myanmar coast; important marine-conservation topic.

features.name: Paharpur
features.detail: Ruins of the Buddhist Vihara at Paharpur; UNESCO World Heritage inscription in 1985.

features.name: Bagerhat
features.detail: Historic Mosque City of Bagerhat; UNESCO World Heritage inscription in 1985.

features.name: Mahasthangarh
features.detail: Archaeological remains associated with ancient Pundranagara; useful for ancient Bengal geography.

features.name: Nile
features.detail: Major northeastern African river system; White Nile and Blue Nile branches.

features.name: Amazon River
features.detail: Major South American river and drainage basin; largest river by discharge.

features.name: Danube River
features.detail: European river draining into the Black Sea.

features.name: Volga River
features.detail: Longest river in Europe; drains into the Caspian Sea.

features.name: Mekong River
features.detail: Transboundary Southeast Asian river; drains into the South China Sea.

features.name: Indus River
features.detail: Himalayan river system draining into the Arabian Sea; central to Indus civilisation geography.

features.name: Tigris and Euphrates
features.detail: River systems associated with Mesopotamia.

features.name: Yangtze River
features.detail: Asia's longest river; flows to the East China Sea.

features.name: Mississippi River
features.detail: Major North American river draining to the Gulf of Mexico.

features.name: Lake Baikal
features.detail: Deepest lake; large freshwater store in Siberia.

features.name: Lake Victoria
features.detail: Large East African lake shared by Tanzania, Uganda and Kenya.

features.name: Lake Titicaca
features.detail: High-elevation Andean lake shared by Peru and Bolivia.

features.name: Lake Superior
features.detail: Largest freshwater lake by surface area; one of the Great Lakes.

features.name: Aral Sea
features.detail: Former large inland lake; severe shrinkage is an environmental-study topic.

features.name: Mount Everest
features.detail: Highest summit above sea level; on the Nepal–China boundary.

features.name: Himalayas
features.detail: Major Asian mountain system; country list is regional rather than a territorial claim.

features.name: K2
features.detail: Karakoram summit; location in the disputed Kashmir region requires control and sovereignty distinctions.

features.name: Andes
features.detail: Major mountain system along western South America.

features.name: Alps
features.detail: Major European mountain region.

features.name: Ural Mountains
features.detail: A conventional component of the Europe–Asia division.

features.name: Sahara Desert
features.detail: Largest hot desert; stretches across North Africa.

features.name: Gobi Desert
features.detail: Desert region of Mongolia and northern China.

features.name: Atacama Desert
features.detail: Very arid desert of northern Chile.

features.name: Kalahari Desert
features.detail: Southern African arid region.

features.name: Arabian Desert
features.detail: Large desert region on the Arabian Peninsula.

features.name: Mariana Trench
features.detail: Western Pacific ocean trench; Challenger Deep is the deepest known ocean-floor location.

features.name: Troy
features.detail: Ancient city in northwestern modern Turkey; a past-question location theme.

features.name: Mesopotamia
features.detail: Historical region between and around the Tigris and Euphrates; not a modern country.

features.name: Mohenjo-daro
features.detail: Indus civilisation archaeological site in modern Pakistan.

features.name: Petra
features.detail: Ancient Nabataean city in modern Jordan.

features.name: Angkor
features.detail: Historic Khmer capital region in Cambodia.

features.name: Machu Picchu
features.detail: Inca archaeological site in Peru.

features.name: Greenwich
features.detail: Prime-meridian reference. Ideal solar-time rule: 15 degrees longitude = one hour; civil time zones can differ.

features.name: Korean Military Demarcation Line
features.detail: Military Demarcation Line established by the 27 July 1953 armistice at the line of contact; the DMZ is a zone around this line. It is not simply the 38th parallel.

features.name: Golan Alpha Line
features.detail: Western limit of the 1974 Area of Separation under the Israel–Syria disengagement arrangements. The agreement is not a final peace or sovereignty settlement; historical agreement geometry does not establish current deployments.

features.name: Golan Bravo Line
features.detail: Eastern limit of the 1974 Area of Separation. Alpha and Bravo are separate reference lines in the disengagement framework; source geometry is a generalised agreement snapshot, not live military control.

features.name: Western Sahara berm
features.detail: A defensive berm associated with the Western Sahara conflict and MINURSO monitoring context. It is not an internationally agreed sovereign border. The 1991 ceasefire broke down in 2020; this record is not a live frontline map.

features.name: Kashmir Working Boundary
features.detail: A reference used in the India–Pakistan Jammu and Kashmir context, distinct from the northern Line of Control. Terminology reflects the relevant parties and UN monitoring context.

features.name: Actual Ground Position Line (Siachen)
features.detail: Military-position reference associated with the Siachen region. Do not extend the agreed Line of Control beyond NJ9842 and label the extension as the same agreed line. This atlas uses a regional marker for the AGPL.

organisations.name: SAARC
organisations.full: South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation

organisations.name: BIMSTEC
organisations.full: Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation

organisations.name: ASEAN
organisations.note: 11 members: Timor-Leste joined on 26 October 2025. Older answer keys may say 10.

organisations.name: D-8
organisations.note: 9 members despite the name: Azerbaijan accepted in 2024 and completed full-membership ratification in 2025.

organisations.name: NATO
organisations.note: 32 members; Finland joined in 2023 and Sweden in 2024.

organisations.name: EU
organisations.hq: Brussels; institutions also in Luxembourg and Strasbourg
organisations.note: 27 member states; distinguish EU membership from euro-area membership.

organisations.name: GCC
organisations.full: Cooperation Council for the Arab States of the Gulf

organisations.name: UN
organisations.note: 193 member states. The Holy See and State of Palestine are non-member observer states. Charter signed 26 June; entered into force 24 October 1945.

organisations.name: BRICS
organisations.hq: Rotating presidency; no permanent central secretariat
organisations.note: 11 countries listed by Brazil’s official BRICS presidency source; first leaders’ summit in 2009. Saudi Arabia’s formal participation has been described inconsistently in other sources. This filter follows the cited presidency list, and does not equate partner countries with members.

organisations.name: OPEC
organisations.full: Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries
organisations.note: Dated study list: excludes the UAE following its official announcement of withdrawal effective 1 May 2026. The OPEC website still lists it; this discrepancy is preserved. OPEC+ is a wider cooperation arrangement, not identical to OPEC membership.

headquarters.name: World Economic Forum
headquarters.city: Cologny, Geneva; annual meeting usually in Davos

metadata.geometrySource: Natural Earth 1:10 million, generalised world atlas scale
metadata.capitalCurrencySource: mledoze/countries download, with explicitly annotated corrections
metadata.peopleStatus: Editorial examples with further-reading links; not independently verified for every country
metadata.namedLineGeometry: Approximate markers plus separately selectable, generalised source route context for Korea, Cyprus, Golan and India–Pakistan. Not live frontlines or surveyed treaty limits.
metadata.organisationsScope: Selected complete lists: UN, NATO, EU, BRICS, OPEC, SAARC, BIMSTEC, ASEAN, D-8 and GCC; cited membership-source discrepancies are retained.
metadata.controlLinesSource: Natural Earth 1:10-million land-boundary lines, downloaded 9 October 2026. Original classifications, including “please verify”, are retained.
